paper_metadata.title: The influence of aluminum content on the microstructure and mechanical properties of TiZrHfNbAlx refractory high entropy alloys
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Refractory Metals and Hard Materials

evidence.quote: This study incorporated aluminum into a TiZrHfNb refractory high entropy alloy matrix, fabricating TiZrHfNbAlx (x = 5, 10, 15, 20 at.%) refractory high entropy alloys via vacuum arc melting.

Refractory high-entropy alloy ingots with different Al contents, labeled as TiZrHfNbAlx (x = 5, 10, 15, 20 at.%, corresponding to Al-5, Al-10, Al-15, and Al-20, respectively), were synthesized using vacuum arc melting.

process_steps.input_state: raw materials Ti, Zr, Hf, Nb, Al (purities exceeding 99.9 wt%)

evidence.quote: The smelting procedure is carried out as follows: First, the smelting furnace is evacuated to establish a vacuum environment. Next, high-purity argon gas (99.99 % purity) is introduced into the furnace. The smelting process then begins. To ensure uniform composition, the ingot is remelted ten times with inversion, with each cycle lasting approximately three minutes under a current of approximately 550 A. After smelting is complete, the material is cooled to room temperature, and samples are taken, resulting in a 100 g button-shaped alloy ingot.

The observed increase in hardness with higher Al content can primarily be attributed to the solid solution strengthening mechanism, which causes significant lattice distortion and enhances dislocation pinning [29].
Moreover, the ordered BCC phase in Al-20 alloy significantly enhances hardness through precipitation strengthening mechanisms.

The strengthening effect attributed to grain refinement in refractory high-entropy alloys is relatively minor, with solid solution strengthening and second-phase strengthening identified as the primary strengthening mechanisms.
The significant enhancement in the compressive yield strength of the Al-20 alloy can be attributed to second-phase strengthening.
